From 4007844b05815717f522c7ea9914e24ad0ff6c79 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2020 11:31:35 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] soc: mediatek: Check if power domains can be powered on at
 boot time

In the error case, where a power domain cannot be powered on
successfully at boot time (in mtk_register_power_domains),
pm_genpd_init would still be called with is_off=false, and the
system would later try to disable the power domain again, triggering
warnings as disabled clocks are disabled again (and other potential
issues).

Also print a warning splat in that case, as this should never
happen.

Fixes: c84e358718a66f7 ("soc: Mediatek: Add SCPSYS power domain driver")
Signed-off-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200928113107.v2.1.I5e6f8c262031d0451fe7241b744f4f3111c1ce71@changeid
Signed-off-by: Matthias Brugger <matthias.bgg@gmail.com>

diff --git a/drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c b/drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c
index f669d3754627..ca75b14931ec 100644
--- a/drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c
+++ b/drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c
@@ -524,6 +524,7 @@ static void mtk_register_power_domains(struct platform_device *pdev,
 	for (i = 0; i < num; i++) {
 		struct scp_domain *scpd = &scp->domains[i];
 		struct generic_pm_domain *genpd = &scpd->genpd;
+		bool on;
 
 		/*
 		 * Initially turn on all domains to make the domains usable
@@ -531,9 +532,9 @@ static void mtk_register_power_domains(struct platform_device *pdev,
 		 * software.  The unused domains will be switched off during
 		 * late_init time.
 		 */
-		genpd->power_on(genpd);
+		on = !WARN_ON(genpd->power_on(genpd) < 0);
 
-		pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, false);
+		pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, !on);
 	}
 
 	/*
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-scpsys.c`**
   - A new boolean variable `on` is introduced to track the success of powering on the power domains.
   - The call to `genpd->power_on(genpd)` is modified to check for errors. If it fails (returns a negative value), a warning is printed using `WARN_ON`, and `on` is set to false.
   - The `pm_genpd_init` function call is updated to use the value of `on` instead of a hardcoded `false`. This change ensures that if the power domain was successfully powered on, it will be initialized as such; otherwise, it will be initialized as off.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The introduction of the `on` variable directly relates to the error handling of the `genpd->power_on(genpd)` function. By checking the return value of this function, the patch ensures that the system does not attempt to disable a power domain that failed to power on, thus preventing potential warnings and issues during system operation.
- The modification in the `pm_genpd_init` function call is contingent upon the success of the power-on operation. This relationship ensures that the initialization of the power domain reflects its actual state, thereby improving the robustness of the power management system in the Mediatek driver.

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the system attempts to initialize and subsequently disable a power domain that has failed to power on during boot time. This leads to warnings and potential issues, as the power domain is not in a valid state for the operations being performed on it.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void mtk_register_power_domains(struct platform_device *pdev,
 				struct scp *scp, int num)
 {
 	struct genpd_onecell_data *pd_data;
 	int i, ret;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < num; i++) {
 		struct scp_domain *scpd = &scp->domains[i];
 		struct generic_pm_domain *genpd = &scpd->genpd;
+		bool on;
 
 		/*
 		 * Initially turn on all domains to make the domains usable
 		 * with !CONFIG_PM and to get the hardware in sync with the
 		 * software.  The unused domains will be switched off during
 		 * late_init time.
 		 */
-		genpd->power_on(genpd);
+		on = !WARN_ON(genpd->power_on(genpd) < 0);
 
-		pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, false);
+		pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, !on);
 	}
 
 	/*
 	 * We are not allowed to fail here since there is no way to unregister
 	 * a power domain. Once registered above we have to keep the domains
 	 * valid.
 	 */
 
 	pd_data = &scp->pd_data;
 
 	ret = of_genpd_add_provider_onecell(pdev->dev.of_node, pd_data);
 	if (ret)
 		dev_err(&pdev->dev, "Failed to add OF provider: %d\n", ret);
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
genpd->power_on(genpd);
pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, false);
```
Reason:
The system attempts to power on a power domain using `genpd->power_on(genpd)`, which can fail and return a negative value. If this happens, the subsequent call to `pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, false)` initializes the power domain as if it was successfully powered on, leading to attempts to disable a power domain that is not in a valid state, causing warnings and potential issues.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
on = !WARN_ON(genpd->power_on(genpd) < 0);
pm_genpd_init(genpd, NULL, !on);
```
Reason:
The patch checks if the power domain was successfully powered on by using `WARN_ON` to capture any failure. It then sets the `on` variable accordingly. The `pm_genpd_init` function is called with the correct state of the power domain (`!on`), ensuring that it is only initialized as powered on if the power-on operation was successful, thus preventing the system from trying to disable an invalid power domain.
